predecessors.name: Kingdom of France
predecessors.text: the Huguenot-held coast of Saintonge and Aunis around La Rochelle: Cliopatria's 1622 polygon plus La Rochelle

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the Huguenot enclave's remnant polygon, and La Rochelle, taken in October 1628

ledger.x: 1621: the Huguenots rise against the crown.
10 September 1627: the siege of La Rochelle begins.
28 October 1628: the crown takes La Rochelle, the Huguenots' main stronghold.
1629: the Edict of Ales ends the Huguenots' territorial and military privileges.

wars.name: Huguenot rebellions
wars.outcome: Three small civil wars in south-western France; the Treaty of Montpellier ended the first in stalemate in October 1622 (Siege page), the crown took La Rochelle in October 1628 and the Huguenots lost their territorial, political and military privileges in 1629.

wars.name: Siege of La Rochelle
wars.outcome: The royal army, with a 1,400 m seawall and 12 km of entrenchments, starved the city out: unconditional surrender on 28 October 1628.

certainty.note: A rebel enclave without a boundary: neither page outlines the Huguenot-held land, and the polygon is Cliopatria's.
